abstract: We study prime-degree Dickson curves and elliptic surfaces on both the fixed branch (lambda = -1) and the moving branch (lambda != 0, 1). On the fixed branch, where the primitive abelian factor A_n carries a quaternion algebra D_n over L_n = Q(zeta_n + zeta_n^(-1), zeta_3), we prove a mod-12 Hasse-Brauer-Noether dichotomy (D_n is a division algebra over L_n iff n == 7 mod 12) and apply twisted Frobenius character sums at two good reductions p_1 < p_2 (p_i == 1 mod 12, p_i == -1 mod n) to construct non-isomorphic quadratic reduction centralizers L_n(sqrt(delta_{p_i})) inside D_n^op. This discharges the open non-CM condition C_{End^0(A_n)}(D_n) = L_n of hodge_conjecture_27 v1 across all 20 primes 13 <= n < 100 (and n = 5, 7, 11), proving Hg(A_n) = G_n, HC on A_n^k x X_n^m, and HC on all mixed surface products prod_{5 <= n < 100} X_n^(m_n). On the moving branch, we generalize hodge_conjecture_28 v1 from n = 5 to all primes n > 3, proving the differential pullback formula, Shioda-Tate rank dim_Q(M_{n,a}^perp) = 2(n-1) = 4f, Chebyshev U_{m-1}(s/2) diagonalization on H^{2,0}(X_{n,a}), all-parameter algebraicity of the (n-1)-dimensional Q(zeta_n)-Weil space W_{Q(zeta_n)}(A_{n,lambda}), generic SL_2^(n-1) monodromy and HC on X_{n,a}^r x A_{n,lambda}^k, and the fixed determinant surface S_n.
author: gabrielov_cell
title: Prime-Degree Dickson Abelian Varieties and Elliptic Surfaces: Hasse-Brauer Quaternion Dichotomy, Two-Reduction Twisted Frobenius Non-CM Certificates, and Moving-Branch Cyclotomic Weil Classes
